title: Unified Threat Model: Post-Quantum Secure Messaging, Trusted Access Adapter, and SOC Anomaly Detection

system_overview.scope: End-to-end post-quantum cryptographic prototype covering PQC messaging, access control, audit integrity, crash recovery, and security anomaly detection.
system_overview.execution_model: Isolated process execution per adapter request reading JSON over stdin and writing JSON over stdout; zero shared memory state.
cryptographic_primitives: X25519 - Classical Diffie-Hellman Key Agreement (Hybrid PQC)
AES-256-GCM - Authenticated Symmetric Encryption with Associated Data
SHA-256 - Cryptographic Hashing and Hash-Chained Audit Ledger
HMAC-SHA-256 - Keyed Proof of Possession and Checkpoint Signatures
HKDF-SHA256 - Symmetric Key Derivation with Transcript Binding

part_c.scope: Core trusted adapter interface, atomic on-disk state store, tamper-evident audit logging, single-commit crash recovery, and post-quantum signed backups.

protected_assets.description: Chronological record of security events and access decisions.
Set of permanently revoked actors, ownership registry, and disabled identities.
Exported archives of state and cryptographic metadata.

security_requirements: confidentiality (disclosed only to authorized non-revoked owners)
stored strictly in local state file
zero leakage to stdout, stderr, or audit logs

trust_boundaries.name: Boundary 1: Adapter Input Interface
threats_mitigated: Malformed JSON and parsing denial of service (1 MiB input cap enforced)
Parameter spoofing (actor identity pinned to validated request['actor'])
Log injection (free-text newlines and fake JSON escaped via canonical serialization)
Diagnostic information leaks (exceptions caught globally, tracebacks suppressed)

trust_boundaries.name: Boundary 2: Local State Storage Directory
threats_mitigated: Concurrent access races (store.py mutex via store.lock)
Mid-transaction crash corruption (write-ahead journal with atomic os.replace)
Audit history alteration (SHA-256 hash chaining and ML-DSA-65 signed checkpoints)

adversaries.name: Malicious / Revoked Client
adversaries.threat: Attempts to read assets post-revocation, inject unescaped newlines/JSON into audit log, or spoof identity via extra fields like actor_id.
adversaries.mitigation: Monotonic revocation enforcement, canonical JSON serialization, strict actor pinning to validated request['actor'].

adversaries.name: Local Process Disruptor
adversaries.threat: Crashes the service mid-transaction during revocation to leave state inconsistent or rollback access revocation.
adversaries.mitigation: Write-ahead journal with single commit point (os.replace); revocations are roll-forward and re-applied idempotently on startup.

adversaries.name: Backup Manipulator
adversaries.threat: Modifies backup contents, attempts rollback to previous key_version, or restores an older backup to un-revoke an actor.
adversaries.mitigation: ML-DSA-65 signed manifest with SHA-256 state digest; restore strictly enforces current.revoked UNION backup.revoked and monotonic key_version.

adversaries.name: Audit Log Tamperer
adversaries.threat: Modifies historical log entries to conceal violations or deletes tail entries to hide recent activity.
adversaries.mitigation: SHA-256 hash chaining across every entry; signed ML-DSA-65 checkpoint binding seq and head hash.

security_controls.defense: Actor identity pinned strictly to validated request['actor']; extra fields discarded.
Canonical JSON serialization encodes free-text values into standard string literals.
SHA-256(prefix || prev_hash || canonical_entry); modifying any field invalidates subsequent hash chain.
Atomic signed checkpoint.json binds current seq and head hash using ML-DSA-65 signatures.
Write-ahead journal with single commit point (os.replace); roll-forward idempotent recovery.
Manifest containing SHA-256 digest signed with ML-DSA-65 verified prior to applying.
Global try/except in track4_service.py catches all exceptions and emits generic error strings.

known_limitations: ML-DSA-65 signing key is stored in TRACK4_STATE_DIR; external head hash anchoring recommended for out-of-band anchoring.
Single-node crash recovery semantics; multi-node consensus out of scope for Part C adapter.
Protected read interface provides zero body disclosure on deny, auditing all attempts.

part_a.scope: Post-Quantum Secure Messaging & Protected Read Interoperability

protected_assets.description: Directional AES-256-GCM symmetric session keys derived via HKDF.
ML-KEM-768 encapsulated secret and HMAC-SHA256 proof over challenge and stored body.
security_requirements: proof tied to challenge and stored body
zero disclosure of raw shared secret

trust_boundaries.name: Untrusted Network Wire
threats_mitigated: Passive wiretapping (thwarted by hybrid ML-KEM-768 + X25519 key encapsulation)
Packet replay (atomic tracking in messaging_replay_state.json rejecting duplicated counters)
Tampering with headers or ciphertext (AES-256-GCM authenticated tag and AAD header binding)
Destination tampering (handshake signs sender and recipient with ML-DSA-65)

adversaries.name: Passive Network Eavesdropper
adversaries.threat: Intercepts packets on the network wire to read plaintext or harvest traffic for future quantum cryptanalysis.
adversaries.mitigation: Hybrid post-quantum key exchange (ML-KEM-768 + X25519) with AES-256-GCM authenticated encryption.

adversaries.name: Active Network Replayer & Tamperer
adversaries.threat: Replays past valid packets, modifies ciphertext bytes, or alters destination headers.
adversaries.mitigation: Atomic replay tracking in messaging_replay_state.json rejecting duplicated counters; AES-256-GCM authentication tag and AAD header binding.

adversaries.name: Post-Handshake Key Compromiser
adversaries.threat: Steals long-term identity keys after session completes to decrypt historical transcripts.
adversaries.mitigation: Ephemeral key exchange; private keys zeroed immediately post-handshake and symmetric keys wiped on close_session().

goals_verification.mechanism: Atomic persistence to messaging_replay_state.json tracking (session_id, receiver_scope, counter).
Handshake signs sender and recipient with ML-DSA-65 and binds them into HKDF transcript; receive() checks header recipient as AES-256-GCM AAD.
Session keys derived via HKDF-SHA256 from fresh ephemeral X25519 and ML-KEM-768 shared secrets; close_session() zeroes symmetric keys in memory.
Chunks authenticated on arrival, buffered by (session_id, msg_id) and chunk_index, expired after timeout via expire_incomplete().
Encapsulates with Base64 ML-KEM-768 public key, returning Base64 ciphertext and lowercase 64-hex HMAC-SHA-256 proof over challenge + body.

known_limitations: No per-message ratcheting during an active open session.
Pre-handshake ML-DSA-65 identity key theft permits MITM impersonation on new handshakes.
Wire metadata (headers, chunk counts, ciphertext size) remains unencrypted.

detector.scope: Deterministic Cybersecurity Anomaly Detection & Uncertainty-Aware SOC Pipeline

protected_assets.description: Integrity of privilege modifications and administrative role changes.
security_requirements: all role changes must bind to valid approved tickets in approvals registry

protected_assets.description: Authorized lateral communication paths between microservices.
security_requirements: unauthorized service hops must be immediately flagged upon first traversal

protected_assets.description: True chronological sequence of distributed events despite clock offset.
security_requirements: bounded clock skew compensation (+/-120s) and explicit uncertainty tagging

rules.threat: Privilege escalation by unauthorized actors or role changes without valid approval ticket.
rules.defense: Deterministic cross-reference against simdata/approvals.json ensuring approval status, actor, and role match.

rules.threat: Intruder hopping between services along unobserved or unauthorized pathways.
rules.defense: Actor profile tracking with immediate first-path violation alerts.

rules.threat: Exfiltration or credential harvesting characterized by sudden bursts in data read activity.
rules.defense: Sliding window rate monitoring against baseline threshold with alert cooldown.
